Remove bonus scoring in the final five-minute block.
Record team and individual behaviours after the activity.
coachingPoints: Players must recognise possession change despite contact and congestion.
The ball winner should secure possession before expanding.
The nearest defender applies immediate legal pressure.
Supporting defenders recover, fold and protect dangerous space.
Repeat pressure must continue until structure is restored.
Attacking players should create clear close and outside releases.
Exit decisions must match pressure, support and field position.
Players must react to marks, spoils, tackles and loose footballs.
Work rate should remain tactically organised.
Behaviours must continue when bonus scoring is removed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Recognition speed during contested turnovers.
Body position and possession security.
Quality of the first disposal.
Nearest-player pressure.
Defensive recovery when outnumbered.
Ability to escape congestion.
Repeat defensive pressure.
Switch support after pressured regains.
Reactions following tackles and aerial contests.
Quality of exit decisions.
Whether structure survives fatigue.
Whether behaviours remain during unrestricted play.

commonErrors.error: Players lose awareness during contact.
commonErrors.correction: Scan before entering the contest and communicate throughout it.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal is rushed or blind.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and identify a receiver with reduced pressure.

commonErrors.error: Defenders apply one effort and stop.
commonErrors.correction: Require pressure transfer and repeated defensive action.

commonErrors.error: Recovering defenders chase instead of protecting central space.
commonErrors.correction: Delay the attack and recover goal-side.

commonErrors.error: Players force a predetermined exit.
commonErrors.correction: Read pressure, support and turnover consequence.

commonErrors.error: Behaviours disappear without bonus scoring.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce transition principles as permanent match habits.

progressions: Expand to full-ground match simulation.
Allow match-like legal contact.
Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Create temporary numerical imbalances.
Start transitions from stoppages, kick-ins and forward entries.
Use positional assessment standards.
Record the activity for video review.
regressions: Reduce field size and player numbers.
Assess only four contested transition behaviours.
Reduce contact and running demands for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Apply immediate and repeat defensive pressure.
React correctly after tackles and aerial contests.
Maintain structure and effort under fatigue.
matchApplication: This assessment tests transition performance in the contested conditions that dominate Australian football. It determines whether players can preserve decision quality, structure and work rate when possession changes through pressure rather than clean, predictable ball movement.

title: Smother-to-Surge Transition
primarySkill: Transitioning immediately after a successful smother.
objective: Develop coordinated reactions after a smother so the defending team secures the loose football and attacks before the opposition can recover.
groundSize: 35 metres long × 30 metres wide with a smother zone and scoring gate at each end.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central smother zone approximately 12 metres × 12 metres.
Place one scoring gate at each end of the wider area.
Divide players into two teams of four to eight.
Begin one attacking player with the football inside the smother zone.
Position one active defender and supporting players from both teams around the zone.
Rehearse safe smother technique before live play.
The coach stands outside the area with spare footballs.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking player receives and prepares to kick from inside the smother zone.
The defender approaches under control and attempts a legal smother.
If the kick clears the defender, play continues towards the attacking gate.
If the football is smothered, all players react to the loose-ball location.
The team completing the smother attempts to secure possession and counterattack towards the opposite gate.
The former attacking team applies immediate nearest-player pressure.
One point is awarded for completing the smother.
One additional point is awarded for securing the loose football.
Two points are awarded for completing the first disposal and reaching the opposite gate.
Reset after a score, turnover, stoppage or 25 seconds.
coachingPoints: The smothering player must approach safely and remain balanced.
Supporting defenders should anticipate where the football may deflect.
The smothering player must regain the feet and continue into the next action.
The team winning the loose football should secure possession before spreading.
Former attackers must transition immediately rather than appealing for a free kick.
Support should form in front, beside and behind the ball winner.
Players should avoid blindly kicking the smothered football from congestion.
Communication must identify possession and available release options.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Safety and timing of the smother attempt.
Whether players anticipate the football’s deflection.
Whether the smothering player continues after contact.
Whether the first possession is secured.
Whether the former attacking team applies immediate pressure.
Whether the counterattacking team creates separated outlets.
Whether players remain composed around the loose football.

commonErrors.error: The defender dives recklessly at the kicker.
commonErrors.correction: Approach under control, protect the head and use safe smother technique.

commonErrors.error: Players watch the smother instead of tracking the football.
commonErrors.correction: Read the deflection and move to likely recovery space.

commonErrors.error: The smothering player remains on the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Recover the feet immediately and become pressure or support.

commonErrors.error: The loose football is kicked blindly.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and find a clear release.

commonErrors.error: Former attackers stop after the smother.
commonErrors.correction: Apply nearest-player pressure immediately.

progressions: Allow full live play before the kick.
Add a second defender closing from another angle.
Reduce the smother zone.
Introduce match-like controlled tackling after the smother.
Continue play through repeated turnovers.
Add a five-second counterattack bonus.
regressions: Use a smother pad rather than a live football.
Give the smothering team an extra support player.
Reduce repeat efforts for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Apply immediate pressure after losing possession.
Convert the smother into a controlled counterattack.
matchApplication: A smother creates an unpredictable loose football and an immediate transition opportunity. Teams that anticipate the deflection and secure possession can attack while the opposition is still committed to its original disposal pattern.

title: Boundary Contest Rebound
primarySkill: Rebounding from a contested possession near the boundary.
objective: Develop the ability to secure a boundary-side contest and transition into open space without forcing a high-risk central disposal.
groundSize: 40 metres long × 30 metres wide with a narrow boundary contest lane and two exit gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a five-metre-wide contest lane along one boundary.
Place a safe boundary exit gate ahead of the contest.
Place a higher-value central release gate on the opposite side of the area.
Divide players into two teams.
Position three to five players from each team near the contest lane.
Position outside support players through the central and far-side space.
The coach begins each repetition with a ground ball, high ball or pressured pass into the boundary lane.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both teams contest for the football inside the boundary lane.
The team gaining possession must establish control before selecting an exit.
A nearby teammate provides a safe down-the-line option.
Central and far-side players provide release options away from the boundary.
The boundary gate scores one point.
The central release gate scores three points but may only be used when the receiver has clear separation.
A central turnover gives the opposition three points.
The team losing possession applies immediate pressure and attempts to trap the football near the boundary.
Play continues until an exit, turnover, stoppage or 30-second limit.
Alternate the starting boundary after four repetitions.
coachingPoints: Secure possession before attempting to move away from the boundary.
The safe down-the-line option should remain available.
Central release should be used only when the lane is genuinely clear.
Support players must not all enter the boundary congestion.
The ball winner should protect the football from boundary-side pressure.
Players behind the football should provide a reset.
The defending team should use the boundary as an extra defender.
Far-side players must remain engaged as potential switch options.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Body positioning near the boundary.
Whether the ball winner protects possession.
Whether safe and aggressive exits are both available.
Whether players force central disposals.
Whether outside support stays separated.
Whether defenders trap the football against the boundary.
Whether the team can later access central space after securing possession.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt an immediate blind disposal into the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the football and confirm the central receiver is clear.

commonErrors.error: All teammates crowd the boundary contest.
commonErrors.correction: Keep outside players in release positions.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier steps over the boundary unnecessarily.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the football while maintaining awareness of the line.

commonErrors.error: Players ignore the safe down-the-line option.
commonErrors.correction: Retain a boundary outlet when the centre is closed.

commonErrors.error: Defenders allow an easy inside release.
commonErrors.correction: Pressure from the corridor side and force play towards the line.

progressions: Reduce the contest-lane width.
Add full controlled tackling.
Remove the marked exit gates.
Require a switch after a successful boundary exit.
Add a recovering defender in central space.
Continue into a full-ground transition phase.
regressions: Give the ball-winning team an extra outside player.
Stop briefly after possession is secured.
Reduce contact for younger or returning players.
successIndicators: Secure contested possession near the boundary.
Use central space only when clearly available.
Escape the boundary pressure with retained possession.
matchApplication: Boundary contests reduce space and often attract numbers. Teams must secure the football, maintain a safe outlet and recognise when central space is genuinely available rather than forcing a dangerous release.

title: Central Turnover Counterpress
primarySkill: Applying immediate collective pressure after losing possession in the corridor.
objective: Develop an aggressive but organised counterpress that prevents the opposition from exploiting a central turnover.
groundSize: 45 metres long × 35 metres wide with a 15-metre central turnover zone.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a central corridor zone approximately 15 metres wide.
Place one scoring gate at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Begin one team moving the football through the central zone.
Position both teams across the full width of the field.
The coach stands beside the central zone with spare footballs.
Establish a four-second counterpress window.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team attempts to move through the central zone towards its scoring gate.
If possession is lost inside the central zone, the former attacking team begins a four-second counterpress.
The nearest player pressures the new ball carrier.
The next two defenders close the short forward and lateral options.
Deeper players fold behind to protect the direct scoring route.
The counterpressing team receives one point for forcing a backwards disposal.
It receives two points for creating a stoppage and three points for regaining possession within four seconds.
The new attacking team receives three points for escaping the counterpress and reaching its scoring gate.
If the turnover occurs outside the central zone, normal transition rules apply.
Reset after a score, stoppage or 30 seconds.
coachingPoints: Central turnovers require an immediate coordinated response.
The nearest player must close the ball carrier without being sidestepped.
Supporting defenders should take away the first escape options.
The counterpress must include protection behind the initial pressure.
Players should compress towards the turnover without all entering the same contest.
Communication should identify pressure, exit lanes and deeper danger.
The four-second effort must remain tactically organised.
If the opposition escapes, players must immediately recover into normal defensive structure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Reaction speed after the central turnover.
Whether the nearest player applies controlled pressure.
Whether short forward and lateral exits are covered.
Whether deeper defensive protection remains.
Whether several players overcommit to the ball.
Whether the team regains possession or forces a backwards disposal.
Whether players recover when the counterpress is broken.

commonErrors.error: Players react individually rather than collectively.
commonErrors.correction: Assign nearest pressure, first outlet and deeper cover responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Multiple players tackle the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Keep supporting defenders on escape options.

commonErrors.error: The team counterpresses with no protection behind.
commonErrors.correction: Retain a deeper layer to protect the scoring route.

commonErrors.error: Players continue pressing after the opposition escapes.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise the broken press and recover goal-side.

commonErrors.error: Pressure approaches are reckless.
commonErrors.correction: Close quickly, then shorten steps and maintain balance.

progressions: Reduce the central-zone size.
Allow full match-like legal contact.
Give the team winning possession an extra player.
Extend play through multiple turnovers.
Add scoreboard consequences for central turnovers.
Remove the marked central zone.
regressions: Extend the counterpress window to six seconds.
Give the counterpressing team a numerical advantage.
Pause and assign roles after the turnover.
Reduce repetition length for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Regain possession or create a stoppage.
Recover when the counterpress is broken.
matchApplication: A corridor turnover exposes the shortest route to goal. An immediate coordinated counterpress can prevent the opposition from using open central space and may create a second attacking opportunity.
relatedDrills: TR-014 – Stop the First Forward Disposal

title: Failed Overlap Recovery
primarySkill: Recovering defensively after an attacking overlap breaks down.
objective: Develop immediate defensive reactions when an attacking overlap is intercepted, fumbled or otherwise fails.
groundSize: 45 metres long × 30 metres wide with two overlap channels and scoring gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark one overlap channel on each side of the playing area.
Place a scoring gate at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Begin one team in possession in the middle.
Position wide players near the overlap channels.
The coach stands outside the area with spare footballs.
Encourage attacking overlap runs during the first phase.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team attempts to create an overlap and move through a side channel.
The first disposer runs past the receiver.
Defenders attempt to track, pressure or intercept the overlap disposal.
If the overlap succeeds, play continues towards the scoring gate.
If the overlap fails, the original attacking team immediately transitions into defence.
The player nearest the turnover applies pressure.
The failed overlap runner recovers through the corridor or towards the deepest dangerous space.
The new attacking team attempts to score through the opposite gate.
Bonus points are awarded when the failed overlap runner contributes to the defensive recovery.
Reset after a score, turnover or 30 seconds.
coachingPoints: Overlap runners must anticipate the risk of a failed disposal.
The player who ran beyond the football must recover immediately.
The nearest player applies pressure while others protect the corridor.
Players should not stop to express frustration after a skill error.
Recovery runs should be angled towards dangerous space.
The team should retain some balance behind the overlap.
Communication should identify the deepest exposed opponent.
Players must work both ways after aggressive attacking movement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the attacking team preserves balance behind the overlap.
Whether players react immediately when the overlap fails.
The recovery effort of the overlapping runner.
Whether the nearest player pressures the new ball carrier.
Whether the corridor and deepest space are protected.
Whether players show frustration instead of reacting.
Whether the new attacking team exploits the failed overlap.

commonErrors.error: The overlapping runner remains ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Turn immediately and recover towards goal-side space.

commonErrors.error: Players blame the disposal error.
commonErrors.correction: Make the next defensive action the priority.

commonErrors.error: Everyone chases the new ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Use nearest-player pressure with corridor recovery behind it.

commonErrors.error: No player remains behind the overlap.
commonErrors.correction: Retain a safety player during aggressive attacking movement.

commonErrors.error: Recovery runs follow direct opponents into wide space.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the corridor and deepest threat first.

progressions: Allow full tackling.
Remove the overlap channels.
Create a numerical advantage for the counterattacking team.
Add a ten-second scoring target after the failed overlap.
Continue through multiple transition phases.
Introduce full-ground overlap patterns.
regressions: Predetermine when the overlap will fail.
Give the recovering team an extra defender.
Reduce running requirements for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Apply pressure to the new ball carrier.
matchApplication: Aggressive overlap running can expose a team if the disposal fails. Players must immediately reverse direction, protect central space and prevent the opposition exploiting numbers ahead of the football.

title: Second-Possession Transition
primarySkill: Controlling the second possession after a turnover.
objective: Develop coordinated support and decision making so the team retains the football beyond the first possession and first disposal after a regain.
groundSize: 35 metres long × 30 metres wide with four outside scoring gates.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a central possession area approximately 20 metres × 20 metres.
Place one scoring gate outside each side.
Divide players into two teams.
Position players inside and around the central area.
The coach begins each repetition with a loose, intercepted or contested football.
Mark scoring values for the first possession, first disposal and second possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into the central area.
One team secures the first possession.
The ball winner completes a first disposal to a teammate.
The receiver must protect and control the second possession.
Only after the second possession is secured may the team exit through a scoring gate.
One point is awarded for the first possession.
One point is awarded for completing the first disposal.
Two points are awarded for securing the second possession.
Two additional points are awarded for exiting through a gate.
If the football turns over at any stage, the scoring sequence restarts for the other team.
coachingPoints: The first receiver must be selected for their ability to continue the play.
The first disposal should reduce pressure rather than transfer it.
Support must be organised for the second possession.
Receivers should scan before the football arrives.
Players must avoid celebrating the initial regain.
The team should begin spreading while the second possession is being secured.
The second receiver should have forward, lateral and safety options.
Communication must continue beyond the first disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Quality of the first possession.
Whether the first disposal reaches a suitable receiver.
Pressure on the second-possession player.
Whether support exists around the receiver.
Whether the team spreads too early.
Whether communication continues after the first disposal.
Whether possession is retained through the exit.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal goes to a stationary player under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Select a moving receiver with time and support.

commonErrors.error: Teammates stop after the first possession is won.
commonErrors.correction: Make the second possession the major scoring action.

commonErrors.error: Players spread before providing close support.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the second possession before expanding fully.

commonErrors.error: The second receiver disposes blindly.
commonErrors.correction: Scan before receiving and identify the next option.

commonErrors.error: The team exits immediately without control.
commonErrors.correction: Require two stable possessions before a gate can score.

progressions: Increase defensive pressure.
Reduce the central area.
Require the second possession to move forward when appropriate.
Close one scoring gate after the first disposal.
Continue into a larger transition phase.
Introduce full controlled tackling.
regressions: Remove defenders after the first possession.
Allow more time before pressure begins.
matchApplication: Many teams win a turnover but lose the football with the next disposal. Effective transition requires control of the second possession so the initial regain becomes a sustainable attacking phase.

title: Delayed Pressure Trap
primarySkill: Delaying the ball carrier before trapping the next receiver.
objective: Develop coordinated defensive transition in which the first defender delays the ball carrier and teammates pressure the most likely next receiver.
groundSize: 40 metres long × 35 metres wide with three exit channels.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the playing area into one central and two wide exit channels.
Place a scoring gate at the far end of each channel.
Divide players into two teams.
Begin with a live turnover near one end.
Position one defender close to the new ball carrier.
Position supporting defenders between the ball carrier and likely receivers.
The coach varies the available escape channel.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team gains possession and attempts to escape through any channel.
The nearest defender closes the ball carrier but prioritises delay over an immediate tackle.
Supporting defenders identify the most likely first receiver.
As the disposal is made, the supporting defender closes the receiver aggressively.
The original pressure player folds behind the new pressure.
The defending team receives one point for delaying the first disposal.
Two points are awarded for trapping the receiver against pressure.
Three points are awarded for a turnover or stoppage.
The attacking team receives three points for escaping through a gate.
Reset after an exit, turnover, stoppage or 25 seconds.
coachingPoints: The first defender must control the ball carrier’s speed and preferred direction.
Supporting defenders should read likely disposal options.
Pressure transfers as the football moves.
The first pressure player must fold behind the second effort.
Defenders should avoid attempting low-percentage intercepts that open the field.
The trap should form around space, boundary and teammates.
Communication must identify the target receiver.
The defence must remain balanced if the expected disposal is not used.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the first defender delays effectively.
Whether supporting defenders identify the likely receiver.
Timing of pressure on the next possession.
Whether the original defender folds behind.
Whether the defence overcommits to one option.
Whether the attacking team recognises and avoids the trap.
Whether the defensive structure remains connected.

commonErrors.error: The first defender dives in for an immediate tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Control the ball carrier and allow the team trap to develop.

commonErrors.error: The supporting defender leaves the receiver too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold position until the disposal decision becomes clear.

commonErrors.error: The original pressure player stops after the first disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Fold behind and protect the receiver’s escape.

commonErrors.error: Defenders overcommit to a predicted disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain balance and respond to the actual option selected.

commonErrors.error: The trap forms too far from support.
commonErrors.correction: Keep pressure and cover distances connected.

progressions: Remove the marked channels.
Add full match-like contact.
Give the attacking team an extra player.
Start turnovers closer to the scoring gate.
Continue through repeated pressure transfers.
Introduce boundary-side and corridor-side traps.
regressions: Give the defending team a numerical advantage.
Pause after the turnover and assign roles.
Reduce repetition duration for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Transfer pressure at the correct time.
matchApplication: The first defender cannot always win the football. Delaying the ball carrier can direct possession towards a receiver who is easier for teammates to pressure and trap.
relatedDrills: TR-014 – Stop the First Forward Disposal

title: Numerical Advantage Release
primarySkill: Exploiting a numerical advantage after winning possession.
objective: Develop fast and composed use of an extra player during transition without crowding the football or wasting the numerical advantage.
groundSize: 40 metres long × 30 metres wide with a scoring gate at each end.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a rectangular playing area with a scoring gate at each end.
Create attacking groups with one extra player, such as four attackers against three defenders.
Position a second group ready to enter from the opposite end.
The coach starts each repetition with a turnover or loose football.
Rotate players through extra-attacker and defender roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach gives the football to the numerically advantaged team.
Attackers attempt to reach the scoring gate.
The ball carrier must draw or commit a defender before releasing where possible.
Support players create width, forward depth and a trailing option.
Defenders delay, protect the corridor and attempt to force extra disposals.
The attacking team receives one point for identifying the spare player.
Two points are awarded for using the spare player to break a defensive line.
Two additional points are awarded for scoring.
Defenders receive two points for delaying until a recovering defender joins.
Reset after a score, turnover or 20 seconds.
coachingPoints: Numerical advantage should create separation, not extra congestion.
The ball carrier should commit a defender before releasing.
The spare player should move into a useful passing lane.
Support players need different widths and depths.
The team should attack before defensive recovery restores equal numbers.
Disposals must lead receivers into space.
Players should avoid unnecessary extra handballs.
Defenders should delay and protect the direct route.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the spare player is recognised.
Whether the ball carrier commits a defender.
Whether attackers maintain spacing.
Whether the spare player receives in motion.
Whether the team attacks quickly enough.
Whether defenders delay effectively.
Whether the numerical advantage is wasted through poor disposal.

commonErrors.error: The extra attacker moves towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Hold separation and provide a clear passing lane.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier disposes before committing a defender.
commonErrors.correction: Carry long enough to create a genuine two-on-one.

commonErrors.error: Attackers use excessive handballs.
commonErrors.correction: Move the football only when it improves the advantage.

commonErrors.error: Players run in one flat line.
commonErrors.correction: Create forward, lateral and trailing options.

commonErrors.error: The team attacks too slowly.
commonErrors.correction: Use a time target before defensive recovery arrives.

progressions: Add a recovering defender entering from behind.
Reduce the playing width.
Allow controlled tackling.
Require the final disposal to be a kick.
Start the advantage from different field positions.
Continue into a second transition phase.
regressions: Shorten running distances for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Convert the advantage into a score or controlled entry.
matchApplication: Turnovers frequently create temporary numerical advantages. Teams must recognise and exploit the spare player before the opposition recovers and restores defensive structure.

title: Numerical Disadvantage Security
primarySkill: Retaining possession when transitioning with fewer players.
objective: Develop composed possession and support decisions when a team regains the football but remains temporarily outnumbered.
groundSize: 40 metres long × 30 metres wide with two safety gates and one attacking gate.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark one attacking gate at the far end.
Mark two safety gates along the side boundaries.
Create a three-attacker versus four-defender starting situation.
Position one recovering attacker outside the field who may enter after five seconds.
The coach begins each repetition with a regain by the outnumbered team.
Rotate all roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The outnumbered team begins with possession after a coach-created turnover.
Players scan the attacking and safety gates.
If a clear attacking option exists, the team may advance immediately.
If pressure is strong, the team can use a safety gate to retain possession.
The recovering attacker enters after five seconds.
The team receives one point for retaining possession until support arrives.
Two points are awarded for using a safety gate and re-entering successfully.
Three points are awarded for reaching the attacking gate.
Defenders receive three points for forcing a turnover before support arrives.
Reset after an exit, turnover or 25 seconds.
coachingPoints: Outnumbered players should not force aggressive forward movement.
The first disposal must reduce pressure.
The ball carrier should protect possession and use available space.
Safety options should remain wide and connected.
Players should communicate the arrival of recovering support.
Boundary movement may reduce turnover consequence.
An attacking option can still be used when a defender overcommits.
Possession security should lead to a later attacking phase.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the numerical disadvantage.
Quality of the first disposal.
Whether safety gates are used appropriately.
Whether players maintain separation.
Whether possession is retained until support arrives.
Whether the team attacks when a genuine opportunity appears.
Whether defenders coordinate pressure to exploit the advantage.

commonErrors.error: Players force a forward disposal into superior numbers.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and wait for support unless the lane is clearly open.

commonErrors.error: Support players move too close to the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width and give the ball carrier space.

commonErrors.error: The team becomes passive after using a safety gate.
commonErrors.correction: Re-enter quickly once support arrives.

commonErrors.error: Players ignore a defender who overcommits.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise and attack newly created space.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal transfers pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Select a receiver with time, space and a next option.

progressions: Delay the recovering attacker for longer.
Reduce the playing area.
Add controlled tackling.
Remove the marked safety gates.
Introduce scoreboard and time scenarios.
Continue into live play after numbers become equal.
regressions: Shorten work periods for Over 35 players.
matchApplication: A team may regain possession while players remain behind the football or out of position. Retaining the football until support arrives can prevent an immediate secondary turnover and create a more sustainable attack.

title: Turnover Chain Decision Matrix
primarySkill: Selecting the correct transition response across different turnover conditions.
objective: Develop adaptable transition decisions based on field position, pressure, numerical balance and available space rather than predetermined movement patterns.
groundSize: 65 metres long × 50 metres wide, divided into defensive, midfield and attacking turnover zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the field into defensive, midfield and attacking turnover zones.
Mark corridor, boundary and safety exit routes.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare scenario cards varying:
Field position
Numerical balance
Pressure level
Score and time
Available exit
The coach selects a scenario before each repetition without telling players the preferred solution.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins play in one of the three turnover zones.
A team gains possession under the selected numerical and pressure condition.
Players assess the field and choose an appropriate transition response.
Possible responses include fast attack, secure possession, switch, boundary exit, counterpress or defensive recovery.
Play continues for 20–40 seconds depending on the scenario.
Teams score for achieving the scenario objective.
Coaches award a decision-quality point when the chosen response matches the field picture.
A poor decision may be penalised even when the skill execution succeeds.
Players briefly explain the key cue behind their decision after selected repetitions.
Rotate field positions and scenario conditions throughout the activity.
coachingPoints: Transition decisions must reflect actual match information.
Field position changes the reward and risk of each option.
Numerical advantage should encourage fast use.
Numerical disadvantage often requires security or delay.
Central pressure may demand a boundary or switch exit.
A forward-half turnover may justify counterpressing.
Communication should help identify numbers, pressure and open space.
Players should avoid repeating the same solution in every scenario.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan before acting.
Recognition of field position.
Recognition of numerical balance.
Whether pressure level influences decisions.
Whether players account for score and time.
Quality of communication.
Whether decisions are adaptable.
Whether players can explain the cue that guided their choice.

commonErrors.error: Players use the same transition response every repetition.
commonErrors.correction: Change scenario conditions and require decisions to reflect them.

commonErrors.error: Players focus only on the football.
commonErrors.correction: Scan numbers, space, field position and pressure.

commonErrors.error: Successful execution hides a poor tactical decision.
commonErrors.correction: Assess decision quality separately from skill outcome.

commonErrors.error: Players wait for coach instruction.
commonErrors.correction: Allow the group to solve the scenario independently.

commonErrors.error: Communication describes events but not actions.
commonErrors.correction: Use calls that identify the required response.

progressions: Add live scoreboard and time scenarios.
Remove zone and exit markers.
Allow match-like contact.
Introduce consecutive scenarios without resets.
Give different information to separate positional groups.
Use video review to compare decisions with available options.
regressions: Provide two possible responses rather than an open choice.
Pause play for a team discussion.
Give the team a numerical advantage.
successIndicators: Explain the reasoning behind their choices.
Adapt when the original option changes.
matchApplication: Transition decisions differ according to where the turnover occurs, how many players are available, how much pressure exists and what the scoreboard requires. Players must solve the actual match situation rather than rely on a single rehearsed pattern.

title: Pressure Transition Assessment
primarySkill: Integrating transition decisions and actions under sustained pressure.
objective: Assess whether players can preserve transition structure, decision quality and skill execution during repeated pressured possession changes.
groundSize: 75 metres long × 55 metres wide with corridor, boundary, congestion and scoring zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a large field with scoring zones at each end.
Mark a central corridor, two boundary lanes and one congestion area.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Position players across defensive, midfield and attacking lines.
Place spare footballs around the field.
Prepare an assessment sheet covering:
Smother transition
Boundary rebound
Central counterpress
Failed-overlap recovery
Second-possession security
Delayed pressure trap
Numerical advantage use
Numerical disadvantage security
Transition decision quality
Repeat effort under pressure
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession and attacks towards its scoring zone.
Play continues through all natural turnovers.
The coach periodically introduces a scenario involving a smother, boundary contest, central turnover, failed overlap or numerical imbalance.
Teams receive one point for entering the scoring zone and two points for scoring.
A defensive bonus point is awarded for an effective counterpress or delayed pressure trap.
An attacking bonus point is awarded for securing the second possession after a regain.
A numerical bonus point is awarded for correctly exploiting or managing a player-number imbalance.
A decision-quality point is awarded when the selected transition response matches pressure, position and support.
Play four blocks of five minutes with one minute of feedback between blocks.
Use a different pressure theme during each block.
Remove all bonus scoring during the final block.
Complete team and individual assessment after the activity.
coachingPoints: Players must recognise the type and location of the turnover.
Immediate pressure must remain controlled and supported.
Central turnovers require counterpressing or rapid corridor recovery.
Failed attacking movements require immediate defensive response.
The team must secure more than the first possession.
Numerical advantage should be exploited before recovery.
Numerical disadvantage should be managed through security and support.
Exit decisions must match pressure and field position.
Communication should organise both attacking and defensive roles.
Transition principles must remain under fatigue and unrestricted scoring.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Reaction to smothers and loose footballs.
Boundary-side decision making.
Counterpress quality after central turnovers.
Recovery following failed attacking movement.
Security of the first two possessions.
Timing of delayed defensive traps.
Use of numerical advantage.
Management of numerical disadvantage.
Adaptability of transition decisions.
Communication under pressure.
Work rate across repeated transitions.
Whether behaviours remain without bonus scoring.

commonErrors.error: Players use maximum speed without tactical organisation.
commonErrors.correction: Link running effort to pressure, cover, support and balance roles.

commonErrors.error: The team regains possession but loses the next disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Assess and reward second-possession security.

commonErrors.error: Central turnovers create panic and multiple chasers.
commonErrors.correction: Establish nearest pressure, outlet coverage and deeper protection.

commonErrors.error: Numerical advantages are crowded.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain separation and identify the spare player.

commonErrors.error: Numerical disadvantages produce forced forward play.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession until support arrives.

commonErrors.error: Behaviours disappear in unrestricted play.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce the principles as normal match actions rather than scoring tasks.

progressions: Expand to full-ground match simulation.
Allow match-like legal contact.
Introduce scoreboard and time scenarios.
Start phases from stoppages, kick-ins and forward entries.
Create hidden numerical imbalances.
Apply position-specific transition assessments.
Record the activity for video analysis.
regressions: Reduce field size and player numbers.
Reduce contact and running load for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Secure the first and second possessions.
Maintain skill and decision quality under fatigue.
matchApplication: This assessment tests whether players can apply transition principles when possession changes are pressured, contested and tactically complex. It prepares the group for the next phase of the chapter, where transition becomes integrated into team ball movement and full-field structure.

title: Forced Error Conversion
primarySkill: Converting an opposition skill error into an immediate attacking transition.
objective: Develop players’ ability to anticipate a pressured opposition disposal, secure the resulting turnover and attack before the opposition can reorganise.
groundSize: 40 metres long × 30 metres wide with one scoring gate at each end.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a rectangular playing area with a scoring gate at each end.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Begin one team in possession under controlled pressure.
Position defenders to influence disposal direction without immediately tackling.
Place the coach on the boundary with spare footballs.
Encourage defenders to anticipate likely kicks, handballs and fumbles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The team in possession attempts to move the football towards its scoring gate.
Defenders apply pressure designed to force a rushed or inaccurate disposal.
When a fumble, missed target, dropped mark or intercepted disposal occurs, the defending team immediately becomes the attacking team.
The player nearest the error secures the football or prevents the opposition recovering it.
Teammates create forward, lateral and safety options.
The new attacking team receives one point for causing the error.
One point is awarded for securing possession.
Two points are awarded for completing the next two disposals.
Two additional points are awarded for reaching the scoring gate.
Reset after a score, turnover, stoppage or 30 seconds.
coachingPoints: Defenders should anticipate where a pressured disposal is likely to travel.
Pressure is successful when it reduces disposal quality, even without a tackle.
The nearest player must attack the loose football immediately.
The team gaining possession should spread as control is established.
The first disposal must avoid returning the football to the pressured area.
Players should distinguish between a genuine turnover and a temporarily loose football.
Former attackers must react defensively rather than showing frustration.
Support should remain connected through the second disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders anticipate pressured disposals.
Whether the nearest player attacks the loose football.
Whether possession is secured before attacking.
The quality of the first disposal.
Whether teammates spread into separated options.
Whether the team retains possession beyond the first action.
Whether the former attacking team reacts immediately.

commonErrors.error: Defenders admire the pressure action instead of recovering the football.
commonErrors.correction: Continue through the error and secure the resulting possession.

commonErrors.error: Players assume a poor disposal will automatically become a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Compete until possession is clearly controlled.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal returns the football to congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Release to a player with space and a clear next option.

commonErrors.error: Teammates run forward before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Provide close support first, then expand.

commonErrors.error: Former attackers stop after making the error.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure to prevent the opposition converting.

progressions: Allow full legal tackling.
Reduce the playing area.
Award extra points for a score created within ten seconds.
Begin with the attacking team holding a numerical advantage.
Continue play through repeated forced errors.
Remove the scoring gates and use full-field direction.
regressions: Give the team winning possession a neutral support player.
successIndicators: Retain possession through the second action.
React defensively after making an error.
matchApplication: Pressure often creates value through fumbles, missed targets and rushed disposals rather than direct tackles. Teams must anticipate these errors and convert them into controlled attacking opportunities.

title: Trapped Receiver Escape
primarySkill: Escaping pressure after receiving the first disposal from a regain.
objective: Develop the ability of the first receiver after a turnover to recognise pressure, protect possession and use support rather than conceding an immediate secondary turnover.
groundSize: 30 metres long × 25 metres wide with three outside escape gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central regain area approximately 12 metres × 12 metres.
Place three escape gates outside the area.
Divide players into two teams.
Position a ball winner, first receiver and two support players for each team.
Position one defender close enough to pressure the first receiver.
The coach begins each repetition with a loose football or controlled turnover.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team wins possession inside the regain area.
The ball winner releases to a designated or naturally available first receiver.
A defender immediately pressures the receiver.
The receiver may evade, release to support or protect the football until an option appears.
Supporting teammates create one lateral option and one safety option.
The team receives one point for completing the first disposal.
Two points are awarded if the receiver escapes the initial pressure.
Two additional points are awarded for exiting through a gate.
The defending team receives three points for forcing a secondary turnover.
Rotate ball-winner, receiver, support and pressure roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: The first receiver must scan before the football arrives.
Receivers should avoid standing flat-footed.
The disposal from the ball winner should place the receiver away from pressure.
Support players must provide different angles.
The receiver should protect the football if an immediate release is unavailable.
Evasion should create space for the next disposal, not delay unnecessarily.
The safety option must remain behind the football.
Communication should identify pressure before possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the receiver scans before possession.
Whether the first disposal leads the receiver away from pressure.
The receiver’s body position under contact.
Whether lateral and safety support are available.
Whether the receiver evades with purpose.
Whether the team retains possession through the escape.
Whether the defender applies controlled pressure.

commonErrors.error: The first receiver waits stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Lead into space and receive while moving.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner passes directly into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Deliver to the receiver’s safe side.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand on the same line.
commonErrors.correction: Create different lateral and safety angles.

commonErrors.error: The receiver tries to beat every defender individually.
commonErrors.correction: Use support when it provides the safer escape.

commonErrors.error: The receiver disposes blindly when contacted.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the football and locate a clear option.

progressions: Add a second pressure defender.
Reduce the size of the regain area.
Remove designated roles.
Require the escape to include a kick.
Continue into a larger transition phase.
Increase contact to controlled match-like pressure.
regressions: Give the receiver an extra support player.
Allow the defender to begin further away.
successIndicators: Escape without conceding a secondary turnover.
matchApplication: The first receiver after a turnover is often targeted by immediate opposition pressure. Securing this second possession allows the team to establish a genuine attacking transition rather than returning the football immediately.

title: Repeated Contest Transition
primarySkill: Maintaining transition awareness through consecutive contests.
objective: Develop players’ ability to repeatedly reassess possession, pressure and support roles when the football moves through several consecutive contests.
groundSize: 45 metres long × 35 metres wide with three connected contest zones.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark three contest zones in a staggered pattern across the field.
Place a scoring gate beyond the final zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Position two to four players from each team near each zone.
The coach stands centrally with several footballs.
Establish safe contact and ground-ball rules.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins with a contested football in the first zone.
The team winning possession attempts to move into the second zone.
A new contest must occur in each zone through a pressured disposal, ground ball or aerial ball.
Possession may change at any stage.
Players must immediately change attacking and defensive roles after each turnover.
One point is awarded for winning each contest.
One point is awarded for completing the disposal out of each zone.
Two points are awarded for scoring after progressing through all three zones.
Play continues until a score, boundary exit or 45-second limit.
Rotate zone starting positions between repetitions.
coachingPoints: Players must reassess possession after every contest.
Winning one contest does not guarantee control of the next phase.
The nearest player applies pressure when possession is lost.
Support players should arrive outside the immediate contest.
Defenders behind the football must preserve balance.
Players should avoid running past a contest before possession is secure.
Communication should identify each new possession state.
Effort and skill quality must remain through repeated actions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise each possession change.
Whether effort continues after the first contest.
Quality of support around each zone.
Whether players run ahead too early.
Whether defenders recover behind the football.
Whether communication remains clear.
Whether skill quality survives repeated contact.

commonErrors.error: Players relax after winning the first contest.
commonErrors.correction: Treat every zone as a new possession battle.

commonErrors.error: Support players enter the same congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside shape and provide release options.

commonErrors.error: Players continue attacking after possession is lost.
commonErrors.correction: Reidentify the new role immediately.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop after one pressure effort.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer pressure and recover to the next contest.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue produces blind disposals.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the work period and prioritise controlled release.

progressions: Reduce the size of the contest zones.
Increase legal contact pressure.
Add a fourth contest zone.
Introduce numerical imbalance in one zone.
Continue immediately in the opposite direction after scoring.
Remove the zone markers.
regressions: Predetermine the possession winner in the first zone.
Reduce repeat efforts for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Complete controlled exits from each zone.
Progress through multiple contests without losing structure.
matchApplication: Australian football frequently involves several contests before one team establishes clear possession. Players must repeatedly transition between attack and defence throughout the entire chain.

title: Pressure from Behind Recovery
primarySkill: Responding to pressure arriving from behind during transition.
objective: Develop awareness and support behaviours that protect a transitioning ball carrier from recovering pressure arriving from behind.
groundSize: 45 metres long × 25 metres wide with three forward support zones.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a long rectangular area with three forward support zones.
Place a scoring gate at the far end.
Divide players into attacking and defending groups.
Begin the attacking team with a defensive regain near one end.
Position one or two recovering defenders five metres behind the ball carrier.
Position support players ahead, beside and behind the football.
Rotate roles after every repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession and transitions towards the scoring gate.
Recovering defenders chase from behind once the first disposal is made.
Teammates must communicate the approaching pressure.
The ball carrier may accelerate, dispose, protect the football or use a trailing support option.
Support players must avoid leading all options directly ahead.
The attacking team receives one point for communicating rear pressure.
One point is awarded for completing a disposal before contact.
Two points are awarded for retaining possession through all support zones.
Defenders receive two points for creating a turnover from behind.
Reset after a score, turnover or 20 seconds.
coachingPoints: Ball carriers must scan before possession and listen to teammates.
Communication should identify the side from which pressure is arriving.
Support behind the football can protect against a chase-down tackle.
The ball carrier should avoid taking unnecessary bounces under pressure.
Disposals must be made before balance is lost.
Recovering defenders should close legally and tackle safely.
Forward support should remain at usable angles.
Players must not assume transition space will remain open.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether teammates communicate rear pressure.
Whether the ball carrier scans before receiving.
Whether the trailing option remains connected.
Timing of disposal under pressure.
Whether the ball carrier protects the football.
Whether recovering defenders tackle legally.
Whether the team retains possession through the chase.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier is unaware of the chasing defender.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate early and scan before receiving.

commonErrors.error: All support runs ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Retain a trailing safety option.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier takes an unnecessary bounce.
commonErrors.correction: Dispose or protect the football before pressure arrives.

commonErrors.error: Teammates call only “pressure”.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the side and distance of the defender.

commonErrors.error: Recovering defenders make unsafe contact.
commonErrors.correction: Approach under control and use legal tackle technique.

progressions: Add a second recovering defender.
Reduce the field width.
Require one bounce before scoring.
Increase contact to match-like controlled tackling.
Remove the support zones.
Continue into repeated end-to-end transition.
regressions: Add a neutral trailing support player.
Shorten chase distances for Over 35 players.
successIndicators: Protect the football when contact arrives.
matchApplication: Counterattacking players are often chased by opponents recovering from behind. Early communication, awareness and trailing support reduce chase-down tackles and secondary turnovers.

title: Forward-Half Turnover Lock
primarySkill: Preventing the opposition from exiting after a forward-half turnover.
objective: Develop a coordinated forward-half transition response that pressures the ball carrier, closes exits and creates repeat attacking opportunities.
groundSize: Forward half of an oval or approximately 60 metres long × 50 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use one forward half of the ground.
Position an attacking team inside and around forward 50.
Position a defending team inside defensive 50.
Mark three defensive exit gates: near boundary, corridor and far boundary.
Begin each repetition with an attacking entry or forward-half possession.
The coach keeps spare footballs near the attacking side.
Establish roles for nearest pressure, outlet coverage and deeper intercept protection.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team attempts to score.
If the defending team gains possession, it immediately attempts to exit defensive 50.
The nearest former attacker pressures the ball carrier.
Other attackers close the short outlet, corridor and switch options.
Deeper attacking players protect space beyond the first defensive line.
The forward team receives one point for forcing a backwards disposal.
Two points are awarded for creating a stoppage or boundary exit.
Three points are awarded for regaining possession and producing a repeat entry.
The defending team receives three points for exiting through a gate under control.
Reset after a score, successful exit, stoppage or 35 seconds.
coachingPoints: The first pressure player must reduce time and vision.
Supporting players should close likely exits rather than all chasing the football.
The corridor exit is the first priority to protect.
The far-side switch must remain covered.
Deeper players should hold intercept positions.
Pressure should direct the opposition towards lower-value space.
If the press is broken, players must recover rather than continue chasing.
Repeat entries should be composed rather than rushed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Speed of the nearest pressure action.
Whether short and central exits are closed.
Whether the far side remains protected.
Whether deeper intercept positions are maintained.
Whether players overcommit to the ball.
Whether repeat possession is secured.
Whether the group recovers when the press is broken.

commonErrors.error: All forwards chase the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Assign outlet coverage and deeper intercept roles.

commonErrors.error: The corridor exit remains open.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise central protection before wide pressure.

commonErrors.error: Far-side players drift towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Hold switch protection until the near side is secured.

commonErrors.error: A regained football is immediately bombed back inside 50.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and select a controlled repeat entry.

commonErrors.error: Players continue pressing after the exit is broken.
commonErrors.correction: Recover goal-side and rebuild defensive structure.

progressions: Allow full match-like contact.
Remove the marked exit gates.
Add defenders beyond the exit line.
Introduce scoreboard and time scenarios.
Continue play to the opposite end after a successful exit.
Start from different forward-turnover locations.

Limit the defending team to handball for the first disposal.
successIndicators: Recover when the lock is broken.

title: Defensive 50 Panic Exit
